sections.html:
Twelve miles west of Columbia, Lexington is both the Lexington County seat and the largest town in the county by population. Since 2000 the town has grown the way a Columbia bedroom community does, so buyers often trade off lake access, school zone and commute time.

U.S. Route 1, known locally as Augusta Highway, cuts through town, and Lake Murray lies just north. Downtown has older properties while the edges hold newer subdivisions, which means one block can look nothing like the next in age, condition and price.

Headcount rose from 9,793 in 2000 to 17,870 in 2010 and then 23,568 in 2020. Housing details:

Housing measureLexington town
Households, 2020 Census9,462
Housing units, 2020 Census10,211
Share of units vacant7.3%
Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 202468.7%
Median home value, 2020 to 2024$297,700
Median gross rent, 2020 to 2024$1,545

Use the median only as a backdrop. Your house gets priced on its condition, its lot and recent sales close by. A home needing a new roof sells under its move-in ready neighbor, whatever the town-wide number says.

Built in 1930, the lake is held back by a dam about 1.7 miles long, roughly 5 miles north of town. It is Lexington's best known landmark and pulls in buyers who want to live near the water.

If your parcel sits close to the shore, expect extra questions about water access, dock permits and flood zone paperwork. Most Lexington houses never touch any of that. Your title company can say which items apply to your lot.

Permit business goes to the Town's Planning and Building Department, found at 111 Maiden Lane. Doors are open Monday to Friday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. Pick the number that fits your question:

  • Main line: 803-356-5938
  • Inspection scheduling: 803-358-7267
  • Code enforcement: 803-358-1589

The same office reviews proposed businesses for land use compliance. Planning a repair ahead of a sale? Ask first whether it needs a permit. An unpermitted porch or addition can come up once a buyer's attorney starts reading records, and a financed deal may stall while it gets sorted out.

One more thing to verify: a Lexington mailing address does not prove your lot is within town limits. Ask the town, since the answer decides whose rules apply.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The county mails the bill, and the payment window under state law opens September 30 and shuts January 15. Late payers pick up 3% right after January 15, 7% more after February 1 and 5% more after March 16.

Ratios differ by use. Your legal residence is assessed at 4% of value, and any other real property at 6%. Owe something from a prior year? Closing attorneys and title companies typically take it out of the seller's proceeds, so an old balance is a nuisance but rarely a dealbreaker.

Real property owners can opt into a county installment plan. It breaks the year into five advance payments, each 16.67% of the prior year's tax, due February 15, April 15, June 15, August 15 and October 15. The remaining balance comes due January 15.

You must get your application in before January 15. The plan leaves out escrowed taxes and personal vehicles, so if your lender already pays the tax bill for you, the plan is not an option.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Lexington County
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Register of Deeds at 212 S. Lake Dr., Suite 301, which also handles mortgages, liens and plats. Searching is available online back to August 1, 1984. Electronic filing works through partners such as Simplifile and CSC.

Since March 1, 2018, taxable or exempt transfers need an affidavit. Do not put Social Security or bank account numbers on a recorded document unless the law demands them. The state deed fee runs $1.85 per $500 of value.

sections.h2: Selling with problems in the way
sections.html:
Owners who try a standard listing in Lexington commonly bump into one of these:

  • A roof or cooling system that a buyer's inspector will point at
  • Past work done without a permit, which the Town's building office may ask about
  • An estate or probate delay after an owner has died
  • Back taxes and penalties from a missed January 15 deadline

Heat is the main wear factor on local roofs and air conditioning, so a unit that has run through many summers is worth having looked at before the first showing. In a cash sale the buyer takes the house as it stands, and any unpaid tax gets cleared at closing.

With no bank involved, nobody orders an appraisal and nobody sends you a punch list. You describe the house, we study it in its current state, and if it works for us the offer arrives in writing. Say yes and you set the closing day while a title company opens the file.

On that day the title company checks the deed, clears whatever you still owe on the mortgage or taxes from the proceeds and records the transfer with the county. Leave the touch-up paint in the garage.

Our buyers look at tired houses, inherited houses and houses with renters. Compare what we offer against what listing would really cost: fix-up money, months of payments and utilities, and the risk that a financed buyer backs out late.

sections.h2: Timeline from first call to closing
sections.html:
Delays in an ordinary sale usually start on the buyer's side, with underwriting, an appraisal that comes in low and repair demands after the inspection. Those steps drop away here. What remains is the title search, payoff letters and whichever date you pick.

Request a payoff figure from your lender sooner rather than later. If an estate owns the house, line up the person who has authority to sign. Those two chores account for most late-moving closings. Once both are done, the remaining steps are routine signatures and a final walk through the house.

A thin folder can save days. Put in your newest tax bill, a mortgage payoff statement if you still owe, permit records for earlier additions and, for an inherited house, the court or estate papers naming who may sign.

Keep copies of everything in one place, because the title company will ask for most of it anyway. Then phone the Town. Two quick answers, whether the lot lies inside the limits and whether any code case is open, remove the usual last-minute surprises.

faqs.q: What county is Lexington, SC in?
faqs.a: Lexington is the county seat of Lexington County. The county handles tax bills and deed recording, while the town handles zoning, permits and code enforcement inside its limits.

faqs.q: When are Lexington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay between September 30 and January 15 to avoid penalties. Miss that window and the bill grows by 3% first, then 7% from February 1, then 5% from March 16.

faqs.q: Can I pay Lexington County property taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if you apply before January 15 and your taxes are not escrowed. Five advance payments of 16.67% of last year's tax fall due between February 15 and October 15, and you settle the balance on January 15.

faqs.q: What does it take to record a deed in Lexington County?
faqs.a: Bring the deed and an affidavit for the transfer, and pay the state fee of $1.85 per $500 of value. The filing office is the Register of Deeds, 212 S. Lake Dr., Suite 301.

faqs.q: Does Lake Murray change how I sell my Lexington house?
faqs.a: It can. Lake-adjacent parcels may involve shoreline, dock and flood questions that other houses do not, so ask your title company about your parcel.
